get.description: Retrieve a page of CRM objects of a specified type. Customize the response by selecting specific properties to return using the `properties` query parameter. This endpoint supports pagination and can include associated object IDs if requested.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The paging cursor token of the last successfully read resource will be returned as the `paging.next.after` JSON property of a paged response containing more results.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

parameters.name: associations
parameters.description: A comma separated list of object types to retrieve associated IDs for. If any of the specified associations do not exist, they will be ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of results to display per page.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned in the response. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

parameters.name: propertiesWithHistory
parameters.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned along with their history of previous values. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored. Usage of this parameter will reduce the maximum number of objects that can be read by a single request.

post.description: Create a CRM object with the specified properties and receive a copy of the object, including its ID. This endpoint is useful for adding new objects to your CRM system with predefined attributes. Documentation and examples for creating standard objects are available.

Location.description: URL of the newly created resource

post.description: Archive a batch of CRM objects by their IDs. This endpoint is useful for moving multiple objects to the recycling bin in a single request, streamlining the process of managing large datasets.

Create a batch of CRM objects of a specified type in HubSpot. This endpoint allows you to create multiple objects in a single request, streamlining the process of populating your CRM with new data. Each object must have the necessary properties defined, and the response will include the created objects along with their IDs.

Retrieve a batch of CRM objects by their internal IDs or unique property values. This endpoint is useful for fetching multiple objects in a single request, which can help optimize performance when working with large datasets. You can specify whether to include archived objects in the response.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

post.description: Update a batch of CRM objects in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to modify multiple objects of the specified type in a single request. It is useful for bulk updates where you need to change properties of several objects at once. The request body should include the objects to be updated along with their new property values.

Create or update a batch of CRM objects by unique property values. This endpoint allows you to efficiently manage multiple objects in a single request, ensuring that each object is either created or updated based on its unique properties.

Permanently delete a contact and all associated content to comply with GDPR regulations. This endpoint allows you to identify the contact by email address using the optional 'idProperty' set to 'email'. If the email address is not found, it will be added to a blocklist to prevent future use.

Merge two CRM objects of the same type in your HubSpot account. This operation combines the properties of the two objects, consolidating them into a single object. It is useful for cleaning up duplicate records and ensuring data consistency.

Perform a search for CRM objects of a specified type using various filters and criteria. This endpoint allows you to retrieve objects based on specific properties and conditions, providing flexibility in querying your CRM data.

This endpoint allows you to retrieve details of a specific CRM object using its internal ID or any unique property value specified by the `idProperty` query parameter. You can control the response content by specifying desired properties through the `properties` query parameter.

delete.description: Move an Object identified by `{objectId}` to the recycling bin. This operation allows you to archive a specific CRM object by its unique identifier, effectively removing it from active use while retaining the option to restore it later if needed.

patch.description: Perform a partial update of an Object identified by `{objectId}`. `{objectId}` refers to the internal object ID by default, or optionally any unique property value as specified by the `idProperty` query param. Provided property values will be overwritten. Read-only and non-existent properties will be ignored. Properties values can be cleared by passing an empty string.
